Conjecture. Canonical \mathrm{SU}(2)_I isospin from the operator-valued \bowtie_K interface (regularised crystal extension)

Conjecture (isospin-Z/2-anti-symmetric closure). Let \beta_A be an atomic braid using the canonical operator-valued interface \bowtie_K. The regularised crystal functional leaves the canonical isospin swap invariant up to a single isospin-Z/2-anti-symmetric residue.

This residue resolves precisely to the substrate flavor split evaluated at q_0:

  \frac{\Delta m}{M_N}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar_q^2 \cdot h \cdot [2]_q \cdot (1 + \hbar_q^3)}{3}
  \qquad \text{(305 ppm against CODATA)}.

The interface coefficient h diverges at q=0. A regularised Cesàro limit extracts the finite remainder. This separates the isospin-invariant substrate background from the structural isospin violation.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring.
